evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We run a girls' education program in northern Nigeria and we're adding a 6-item 'sense of agency' scale to our baseline survey, in Hausa, administered face to face by enumerators. Items: (1) I can make decisions about my own future. (2) When I set a goal, I usually find a way to reach it. (3) People around me listen to my opinions. (4) I have control over how I spend my time. (5) If something goes wrong, I can do something about it. (6) I know where to get help when I need it. Response options: strongly disagree to strongly agree, 5 points. Respondents are 13 to 18, many with little schooling. Items 3 and 4 worry us. Each item is meant to measure perceived control over decisions (1, 4, 5), goal pursuit (2), social voice (3), and access to support (6). Can you draft the cognitive interview script?
evals.expected_output: A cognitive interview script in the output template with probes for all six items, a note sheet, and a rule for which items to fix.
assertions: Every item has at least two probes, and items 3 and 4 have more than the others.
Every probe is an open question, and none states the item's intended meaning.
Uses scripted probes after each item and does not rely on asking the girls to think aloud.
At least one probe asks how the girl understands the five agree/disagree answer options.
Says what the interviewer does if a girl is upset or cannot answer, and states a rule for which items get fixed after a round.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Can you make a cognitive interview script for our survey?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the questions as worded, what each is meant to measure, and who the respondents are, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for the survey questions exactly as respondents will hear or read them.
Asks what each question is meant to measure.
Asks who the respondents are.
Does not write any probe or script.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: We're using the PHQ-9 depression screener in Swahili with refugee adults in a camp setting to decide who gets referred to the mental health team. Our translation is done. Items are the standard nine PHQ-9 items with the 'not at all / several days / more than half the days / nearly every day' options, read aloud. Each item measures a depression symptom over the past two weeks. We want to check comprehension with 10 respondents before we start referrals. Draft the script.
evals.expected_output: The skill writes the script and says a psychometrician or clinician must be involved before any wording changes or referral decisions, because this is a validated screener that decides referrals.
assertions: Writes probes about the two-week period and about the four frequency options.
Says the wording of a validated screener should not be changed on the strength of these interviews without a specialist.
Says that testing comprehension does not validate the scores or the referral cut-off.
Names a psychometrician, clinician, or clinical researcher to consult.
Says what to bring to that specialist.
Says what the interviewer does if a respondent is upset.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: I want to understand why mothers in our program stop coming to the nutrition sessions after the third visit. Can you write interview questions for them?
evals.expected_output: The skill says this is an interview about why people do or do not do something, not a test of survey questions, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says there are no survey questions to test.
Names draft-tdf-interview-guide.
Does not produce a cognitive interview script.
